title: Tottori
dek: A slow culture-and-crab loop through Tottori city's dunes, Kurayoshi's white-walled warehouses, and Misasa Onsen — built around the one bus transfer that has to work for a party of eight.
verified: ⚠ Draft — Pass A (canonical) and Pass B (native-language/resident) research reconciled Aug 26, 2026 for the Oct 20–23, 2026 trip, against operator/official sources: the Kurayoshi↔Misasa transfer (public bus schedule fetched directly, plus a ryokan-shuttle and 9-seat jumbo-taxi alternative for the group's mobility constraint), Sand Dunes (+ dawn crowd reality, camel-commute path), Sand Museum, the Uradome cruise, Shirakabe Dozo-gun, Sanbutsu-ji/Nageiredo (+ seasonal closure, the viewing platform's accessibility detail), Kabuyu bath, Yakiniku Masashige, Menya Hachibee (+ seating/crowd reality), entry rules, emergency numbers, and crab-season timing (matsuba-gani vs. beni-zuwaigani, cross-checked by both passes). A critic pass on Aug 26, 2026 re-fetched the operator timetable and corrected the anchor transfer: the Kurayoshi↔Misasa service is Hinomaru's 上井三朝線 (routes 70/71), last weekday departure 19:25 from Kurayoshi Station — the earlier 19:08 figure belonged to a different Misasa line that does not call there — and the same line's Mitokusan runs are now the car-free access to Sanbutsu-ji. Re-check before travel: the Kurayoshi–Misasa public bus's exact current fare (operator's fare table is a PDF this pass couldn't read) and the specific run times you plan around, Menya Hachibee's hours (no qualifying primary source found), public-transport access to the Uradome cruise departure point, the FX reference rate, and Japan's current US travel-advisory level (travel.state.gov blocked this pass's plain fetch).

entry.visa: Visa-free — up to 90 days for tourism under Japan's reciprocal exemption arrangement
entry.note: Assumed passport — the intake didn't record the party's passport country/countries; confirm and correct if any traveler holds a different passport. Japan MOFA's own visa-exemption page returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt in this pass, so this cites Japan's official JNTO tourism-board page instead.
